verses.text: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Listen carefully to what I understand,
so you will keep good judgment and your lips will hold on to knowledge.
The lips of an unfaithful woman drip with honey. Her words are smoother than oil.
But in the end she is as bitter as poison, as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to the grave.
She does not think about the path of life. Her ways wander, and she does not even know it.
So now, my sons, listen to me. Do not turn away from what I say.
Keep far away from her. Do not go near the door of her house.
If you do, you will lose your honour to others and give the best years of your life to someone cruel.
Strangers will enjoy your wealth, and what you worked for will go to someone else's house.
At the end of your life you will groan, when your body is worn out and wasted away.
You will say, "How I hated being taught! How my heart hated being corrected!
I would not listen to my teachers or pay attention to those who taught me.
Now I am almost completely ruined, in front of the whole community."
Drink water from your own well, fresh water from your own spring.
Should your springs overflow into the streets, your streams into the public squares?
Let them belong to you alone, not shared with strangers.
May your spring be blessed. Enjoy the wife you married when you were young.
She is like a loving deer, a graceful doe. May her breasts always satisfy you. May you always be captivated by her love.
My son, why be captivated by an unfaithful woman? Why hold another man's wife in your arms?
The LORD sees everything people do. He watches all their paths.
The evil things the wicked do will trap them. The ropes of their own sin will hold them tight.
They will die because they would not be taught. Their great foolishness will lead them astray.
